setlist.title: It's A Man's, Man's, Man's World

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (3 reviews): Reviewer's favorite is the monstrous Viola Lee, with Jerry's guitar standing out; Viola Lee is played quite laid back, unlike the reviewer's preferred versions [5][6][12]
- **Deep Elementary Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer names Deep Elem as a personal favorite from this show; Deep Elem is a version like no other, with Jerry feeling the blues [5][14]
- **Dancing in the Streets** (2 reviews): The Dancin' answers Miles's improvisation with the band's own magic and foreshadows later monster versions; Dancin' has Jerry winding the jam up and down for over seven minutes; around nine minutes resembles Mind Left Body [4][6]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (1 other source): A woman is heard singing from about 7:30, absent from the soundboard; tape opens with audience shouts [3]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 other source): Deadbase lists High Time after Rider; the audience tape cuts after the band starts moving into it [1]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer calls the electric Uncle John's solo worth downloading by itself [5]
- **It's A Man's, Man's, Man's World** (1 review): Man's World is good, though other songs are less inspired [12]

## The recordings

- **gd70-04-12.sbd.kaplan.3820.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 114 min; rated 4/5 by 35 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is good, but Bobby is lost in the mix until the organ quiets; a few faint digiskips in Dancin'; Sound quality is crystal clear; This copy has a three-second gap inserted between tracks, which the reviewer found ruinous [1][6][8][11][12][14][15]
- **gd1970-04-12.149.50th.anniv.radiobroadcast.91.3FM.KXCI.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 15 songs; 114 min [2]
- **gd1970-04-12.143493.aud-Schoolgirl-only.taperchuck3.flac1644**: audience recording; 1 songs; 18 min [3]

## Around the show

- The Dead shared the bill with Miles Davis, who was then active with recent albums like Bitches Brew and Live Evil [4]
- Reviewer says Lesh reportedly watched Miles from the side of the stage nightly and was blown away [4]
- Reviewer speculates that Miles Davis being present that night inspired the band to play far above par [8]
- The band sounds tired and ready to leave the stage, though the guitars burn at times [14]
- Reviewer ranks this Dancin' among the finest ever, a peer of the 6/8/69 and 5/2/70 versions [8]
- Reviewer considers this possibly one of the best concerts of 1970 [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-04-12.sbd.kaplan.3820.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Harry Ely; transferred by Seth Kaplan; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [1]. Also: Audience portion covers Casey Jones through Deep Elem; taper believed to be Harry Ely, unverified [1]
- **gd1970-04-12.149.50th.anniv.radiobroadcast.91.3FM.KXCI.flac1644**: source: Pitch and other corrections of prior source gd70-04-12.sbd-aud.kaplan.3820.sbeok.flac16 [2]. Also: This is a 50th-anniversary radio broadcast version on KXCI Tucson, with small fixes and audio massage by Jamie Waddell [2]
- **gd1970-04-12.143493.aud-Schoolgirl-only.taperchuck3.flac1644**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Taperchuck3; source: audience > unk gen > xlII 90 dolby C, tape trade Dec 1984. [3]. Also: Schoolgirl-only audience tape was found in the uploader's collection, mislabeled as 07-10-1970 Fillmore East; It differs from SHN 3820, a soundboard patched with a master audience recording [3]
